content.Title: Red flags for most common forms of cardiac amyloidosis

Clinical: Hypotension or normotensive if previously hypertensive
ECG: Low/decreased QRS voltage out of proportion to LV wall thickness
Laboratory: Disproportionally elevated NT-proBNP relative to degree of heart failure
Echocardiography: Reduced longitudinal strain with apical sparing pattern

Extracardiac_Red_Flags.Columns: Table indicates presence for TTR and AL forms (marked with Xs in table)

Abbreviations_and_Notes.Note: Table modified from cited source; 'Hereditary TTR-CA' explicitly mentioned.
